rationale: Olden/power is a small (622 LOC, 18 functions, ~5.4 KB text) benchmark dominated by hot recursive numeric kernels (Compute_Lateral, Compute_Branch, Compute_Tree, optimize_node), so the table favors cheap, low-risk transforms and gates expensive ones. SUB and SPLIT get high Security/Diversity weights with low RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights since they are nearly free and provide broad baseline obfuscation across all 18 functions, including the hot kernels. FLA receives the highest SecurityGain weight so it concentrates on the large control-flow-dense functions (optimize_node at 1542 B, Compute_Tree, Compute_Branch), where flattening most disrupts static recovery, while its moderate RuntimeCost weight (0.55) reflects that flattening dispatch loops are tolerable in these kernels but should not blanket tiny helpers. BCF keeps a high RuntimeCost weight (0.75) so bogus predicates are applied only to cold or moderately hot functions, avoiding compounding multiplicative overhead in the recursive compute path; its SizeCost weight (0.70) reflects the program's tight text budget. IBR is allowed selectively on hot branches with a moderate runtime weight and elevated CorrectnessRisk weight (0.35) to respect its CFG-rewrite hazard, while ICALL carries the highest CorrectnessRisk weight (0.45) because indirecting calls in this call/return-heavy recursive workload risks both miscompilation-sensitive behavior and call overhead, so it is limited to few, feature-justified sites. IGV is kept as a mid-tier diversity add-on with a modest CorrectnessRisk weight, since power's small global state (grid structures) benefits from indirection without significant cost. Overall the weighting maximizes layered static-analysis resistance (SUB+SPLIT+FLA) while using the cost dimensions to keep the hot recursive path and the 5 KB text footprint within acceptable overhead.
